scope: Proposition 3.3 (Product extension criterion) of the manuscript “Smooth anisotropic uniqueness in the Calderón problem from one boundary patch” (preprints/Smooth-Anisotropic-Uniqueness-in-the-Calderon-Problem-from-One-Boundary-Patch-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 365 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1ec46ed64206d12d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 13. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let ρ be smooth near z0 = (x0, y0), with ρ(z0) = 0 and dxρ, dyρ ̸= 0. Put ai = ∇iρ |∇iρ|2 , H = Hess ρ. Suppose that at z0 H((a1, −a2), (a1, −a2)) + H((v1, v2), (v1, v2)) > 0 (vi ⊥ ai, |vi| = |ai|) . (3.7) Every product solution given on {ρ > 0} near z0 extends to a neighborhood of z0, agreeing on a smaller part of that side. In fact, the construction uses only two compact product sets in {ρ > ϵ} for some ϵ > 0. The neighborhoods and estimates on smaller neighborhoods are uniform under small smooth perturbations preserving the strict hypotheses, provided the data on those compact sets are bounded.
